findings.claim: Conference: no learned model applied to the circuit graph for CDC; no public CDC-ML benchmark with hazard labels
findings.searched: CDC detection machine learning GNN netlist benchmark, 2025-2026
findings.found: Only traditional static/formal CDC verification. One 2025 Springer paper builds a static CDC tool on Yosys netlists (adjacent method, no learning). No GNN-for-CDC work, no public CDC-ML benchmark.
findings.action: none; novelty claim stands as written

findings.claim: Journal: a saturated benchmark loses discriminative power
findings.searched: saturated benchmark discriminative power ceiling effect leaderboard validity
findings.found: Akhtar et al., 'When AI Benchmarks Plateau' (arXiv 2602.16763, Feb 2026): 60 LLM benchmarks, 14 saturation properties, nearly half saturated. Defines saturation as exactly this loss of discrimination. Descriptive survey, LLM domain, no causal construction, no floating-point discussion.
findings.action: Section II rewritten to concede the observation explicitly and state our delta: a causal construction rather than a survey, in a hardware domain with a real deployment distribution. Cited as akhtar2026.

findings.claim: Journal: floating-point non-associativity perturbs DL training
findings.searched: floating point non-associativity reproducibility deep learning training reduction order
findings.found: Shanmugavelu et al. (arXiv 2408.05148, Aug 2024): FPNA across HPC and DL pipelines, accumulation in iterative algorithms, consequences for correctness testing and certification. Framed throughout as RUN-TO-RUN VARIABILITY.
findings.action: Section II rewritten to concede this and state the two separations: (a) ours is not non-determinism -- both orderings are individually bit-reproducible, so there is nothing to pin down; (b) the existing effect is metric variance of a few points, ours moves real behaviour by 0.872 while the metric moves by exactly zero. Cited as fpna2024.

findings.claim: Journal: reduction order is a lever on model BEHAVIOUR, not merely on run-to-run variance
findings.verdict: NOT NOVEL -- established, and closer than we had recorded
findings.searched: Semantic Scholar graph API and arXiv, 19 Sep 2026: 'floating point non-associativity reduction order model selection deep learning'
findings.found: Shanmugavelu et al., Euro-Par 2025 (arXiv 2503.17173) -- the same group as fpna2024. FPNA under asynchronous GPU reduction flips a classifier's output with NO input perturbation; adversarial-robustness results are overstated when reduction order is ignored; and orderings that cause misclassification can be SEARCHED FOR, by Bayesian optimization over external workloads or by a learnable permutation. This is the closest prior work found to date.
findings.action: Section II rewritten again. We now concede outright that 'reduction order is a lever on behaviour' is theirs, and state three separations: (a) theirs is inference-time on one trained model, ours is training-time and yields two different trained models; (b) theirs is adversarial and sought, ours is an arbitrary benign choice already present in a repository; (c) theirs measures how far a metric moves, ours measures that the benchmark does not move at all. Cited as fpna2025, and also cited in Section IX where the 'well known' framing would otherwise understate the prior art.

findings.claim: Journal: the INTERSECTION -- a mathematically-null implementation choice producing near-total behavioural divergence while a saturated benchmark records no difference
findings.verdict: NOVEL as far as these searches reach
findings.searched: both of the above, plus the combined phrasing
findings.found: Nothing combining the two. The saturation literature does not discuss floating-point or implementation order; the FPNA literature does not discuss benchmark discriminative power. Neither exhibits two models with a bit-identical forward pass that disagree on 87% of real inputs. Re-checked 19 Sep 2026 against the Euro-Par 2025 result above: it is inference-time and adversarial, and says nothing about benchmark discriminative power, so the intersection still stands.
findings.action: this is the contribution to lead with; Sections IX and X already do

residual_risk: Second pass, 19 Sep 2026, added the Semantic Scholar graph API and arXiv to the English-language web search, which is what surfaced the Euro-Par 2025 result the first pass missed. IEEE Xplore and the ACM DL still have NOT been queried through their own interfaces, and neither have the DAC/DATE/ICCAD proceedings, where an EDA-specific version of this result would most plausibly sit. A DBLP query was attempted and refused by the service.

The first pass recorded the FPNA literature as framed 'throughout as run-to-run variability'. That was wrong by omission: the same group had already published a stronger, behaviour-level result. A novelty check that reads only the most obvious paper by an author is not a novelty check, and the miss is recorded here rather than quietly corrected.
The saturation literature is moving quickly -- the closest prior work is seven months old. Re-run before submission.
'As far as these searches reach' is the correct strength of the novelty claim, and the paper should not phrase it more strongly than that.
